Done — the full plan is committed as [PLAN_2026-07-18.md](architecture/PLAN_2026-07-18.md) (commit `cab14f1`, which — satisfyingly — went through the new hooks and got its own Change-Id). Here's the shape of it and where I'd most value your reaction.

## Part 1 — CLI completion, sequenced around the running M9 agent

The M9 agent owns `core/embeddings/`, `core/index.ts`, and core's `package.json` until it lands, so the plan is built in waves that never touch those:

- **W1 (can start immediately, zero collision):** `annotate` + the missing `show --history` flag (the agent write path — CLI files only); the R4 fix in `identity/resolve.ts` (replacing whole-tree similarity with changed-path diff overlap); real `relink`/`reconcile` commands, then using `relink` to repair the two miswired commits in this repo; the `config` command; and the cheap MONOREPO_PLAN §5.1 validation — pushing the three refs to a scratch GitHub repo to confirm sync may need no server at all.
- **W2 (after M9 lands and I've re-verified and committed it):** M10 `reindex` → M11 query engine → M12 `ask`/`blame --why`.
- **W3:** one **decision you should own** before M13 sync — the ledger-note merge format. I recommend reformatting note bodies to JSONL (one entry per line), because it makes the `cat_sort_uniq` union-merge conflict-free by construction, versus a custom merge driver that must be installed per-clone and silently breaks where it isn't. Doing it now, while the real-world data is two repos' worth, is far cheaper than later. Then M13, M14 `doctor` (now explicitly auditing `inferred`/orphan rows — the D1 failure class), and `export`.
- **W4:** capture enrichment — mining `reasoning.tested`/`related` from the transcript spans capture already parses.

## Part 2 — the wider system, reviewed against "prove it to a human"

Your MONOREPO_PLAN holds up well in its core judgments: CLI-first, everything wraps `core`, and the sharp observation that a server's *real* differentiated job is shared indexing (the one artifact that isn't cheap to recompute everywhere), with Postgres/pgvector playing to your strengths. I've endorsed all of that unchanged.

What the "prove it's working / let me review my agents" requirement changes:

1. **The human surface should arrive earlier and cheaper than Electron.** I recommend `git for-ai review` — a local React SPA served by the CLI itself, reading via `core` in-process. Its centerpiece isn't `ask`-as-GUI; it's an **agent activity review**: a timeline of what your agents did, each change showing diff-beside-reasoning with `confidence`/`scope_risk`/`reversibility` as visible flags, the session trace as a readable narrative, and — the "prove it" pixel — the *claim next to its evidence* (`tested` entries alongside the spans showing those tests actually running). The desktop package later becomes an Electron wrapper around the same SPA, exactly as your shared-UI-components plan anticipated.
2. **Even before that:** `git for-ai report --since …` — a generated Markdown/HTML digest of agent activity. Nearly free, immediately useful solo, and it forces the "what does a human actually want to see" questions before any UI is built.
3. **New surface I'm proposing: an MCP server, slotted before the network server.** A stdio `git for-ai mcp` exposing `ask`/`blame_why`/`show`/`annotate` as native tools turns any MCP-capable agent into a first-class reader *and writer* of the intent layer — that's the vision's center, and it's thin because it wraps `core` like the CLI does. Recommended slot: right after M12.
4. **The online service isn't a new system** — when/if it happens it's the review UI plus the shared-index server behind auth, with org dashboards and approval workflows. Keeping that identity is what keeps it cheap. Also noted: a `pr-comment` export so intent summaries can land in GitHub PR review, where humans already do their reviewing.

Updated surface order: CLI → MCP → review UI (report first) → shared-index server → Electron → hosted service.

**Open calls for you:** the JSONL reformat (my recommendation: yes, before M13), MCP-before-server (yes), and review-UI-as-local-SPA-before-Electron (yes). If those sit right, I'll start W1 — `annotate` and the R4 fix first — and M9 should land meanwhile.
Starting W1 now. First up: the `annotate` command and `show --history`. Let me read the pieces I'm building on.
`show` already renders all entries with superseded markers — let me check what CLI_REFERENCE says `--history` specifically adds:
One test to adjust. Now making the `show` changes:
Now the `annotate` command itself — the deliberate agent write path:
Let me verify the `diff-tree` flags behave as expected on this git version before writing tests:

body.text: Now the tests for `annotate`, plus the `show --history` test adjustments:

attributes.command: cd C:/src/git-for-ai/packages/cli && pnpm build 2>&1 | tail -5 && pnpm vitest run src/commands/annotate.test.ts src/commands/show.test.ts 2>&1 | tail -12

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git for-ai annotate cab14f1 --summary "Plan approved by project owner: JSONL ledger reformat before M13, MCP server before network server, review UI as local SPA before Electron" --intent "Record the owner's sign-off on PLAN_2026-07-18.md's three open decisions so future sessions/agents treat them as settled" --as human --tested "discussed and approved in session 2026-07-18" && git for-ai show cab14f1 2>&1 | head -20

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git add packages/cli/src/commands/annotate.ts packages/cli/src/commands/annotate.test.ts packages/cli/src/commands/show.ts packages/cli/src/commands/show.test.ts packages/cli/src/bin.ts && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Add `annotate` (deliberate intent write path) and `show --history`

W1 items 1 of PLAN_2026-07-18.md §1.4, closing the §1.3 vision gap: the
ledger's reasoning vocabulary (DATA_MODEL.md §2.5) previously had no
deliberate writer — only passive capture, which fills reasoning.intent
alone.

`git for-ai annotate [<commit|c/change-id>]`:
- agent surface: --stdin JSON partial entry (unknown keys rejected
  loudly so typos never silently vanish into passthrough);
- human surface: flags for summary + every reasoning field; flags
  override stdin;
- scope defaults to the commit's own diff via diff-tree (paths + blob
  SHAs; deletions anchor to the pre-image blob);
- deliberately CALLS resolveChangeId (unlike log/show's non-minting
  reads): a write requires identity, so R5 minting is correct here;
- provenance from author type (closed enum), plus a passthrough
  `annotated: true` marker distinguishing deliberate entries from
  passive capture.

`show --history` (CLI_REFERENCE conformance): default human output now
renders the effective entry with a "N superseded hidden" hint;
--history includes the appended-over entries; --json always carries
every entry. Entry numbering stays append-order stable either way.

Dogfooded live: the plan-approval decision (JSONL before M13, MCP
before server, review-SPA before Electron) is recorded as an
annotation on cab14f1 — `git for-ai show cab14f1`.

28 tests across the two commands, all passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
